faq.q: Is this the official PMP exam course?
faq.a: No. It teaches the core ideas of project management that align with common international practice, but it is not an official exam-preparation course and is not endorsed by any certifying body.
No. The labs use small, relatable projects.
None. The spreadsheet and document labs run in your browser.

activities.title: Write a project charter
activities.objective: Write a one-page charter that sets purpose, objectives, scope, budget and approval.
activities.scenario: A school wants a project to move its library catalogue online. Write the charter.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Project charter'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Purpose, Objectives, Scope, Budget and time, Risks, Approval.
List at least three objectives in a bulleted list, each with a measure.
State what is in scope and what is out of scope.
Give a budget in rupees and an end date.
Keep it between 130 and 320 words.

checks.label: Six sections
checks.explain: A charter has a standard shape.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: Purpose, Objectives, Scope, Budget and time, Risks, Approval.
checks.explain: A natural order from why to sign-off.

checks.label: In and out of scope
checks.hint: Use the words in scope and out of scope.
checks.explain: Saying what is excluded prevents arguments later.

checks.label: A budget in rupees
checks.hint: Write the budget, for example 150000 rupees.

checks.label: Between 130 and 320 words
checks.explain: Short charters get read and signed.

activities.title: Cost a work breakdown
activities.objective: Total task costs, add a contingency and check against a budget.
activities.scenario: The library catalogue project has six work packages with estimated costs. Add a contingency and check the budget.
steps: In D2 work out each package's cost: hours times the hourly rate in B10 (lock B10).
Fill down to D7.
In D8 total the package costs.
In D9 add a contingency: the total times the contingency percentage in B11.
In D10 add the total and the contingency.
In D11 show Within budget or Over budget by comparing D10 with the budget in B12.

checks.label: D2 is the cost of package 1
D4 is the cost of package 3
D11 compares to the budget
checks.explain: A project must stay within its approved limit or ask for more.

activities.title: Build a schedule and find the finish date
activities.objective: Work out start and end days for tasks that depend on each other.
activities.scenario: Five tasks have durations in days and some must wait for others. Work out when each starts and ends and when the project finishes.
steps: Task 1 starts on day 1. In D2 enter its end: start plus duration minus one.
Task 2 starts the day after task 1 ends: C3 = D2 + 1, and D3 = C3 + B3 - 1.
Task 3 also starts after task 1 ends: C4 = D2 + 1.
Task 4 needs both task 2 and task 3: C5 = MAX(D3, D4) + 1.
Task 5 starts after task 4. In B9 find the project's last day with MAX.

checks.label: D2 is the end of task 1
checks.explain: End day equals start plus duration minus one.

checks.label: C3 starts task 2 after task 1
checks.hint: Add 1 to the end day of task 1 (D2).
checks.explain: Start the day after the predecessor ends.

checks.label: D3 is the end of task 2
D4 is the end of task 3
C5 waits for both predecessors
checks.explain: A task starts after the later of its predecessors finishes.

checks.label: D6 is the end of task 5
checks.explain: The last task decides the finish date.

checks.label: B9 is the project's last day

activities.title: Define roles with a RACI list
activities.objective: State who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for key tasks.
activities.scenario: For the library catalogue project, write a RACI list for three tasks.
steps: Add a Heading 2 for each of three tasks.
Under each, write four lines starting with Responsible:, Accountable:, Consulted: and Informed:.
Name a different person for each line where sensible.

checks.label: Informed lines
checks.explain: Others are kept up to date.

checks.label: Between 40 and 200 words
checks.explain: A RACI should be quick to read.

activities.title: Score a risk register
activities.objective: Score risks by probability and impact and rank them.
activities.scenario: The project team listed five risks with probability (1-5) and impact (1-5). Score them and flag the serious ones.
steps: In D2 enter the score: probability times impact. Fill down to D6.
In E2 show High if the score is 15 or more, Medium if 8 or more, otherwise Low (nested IF). Fill down.
In B8 find the highest score with MAX.
In B9 count the High risks with COUNTIF.

checks.label: E2 is High
checks.explain: A nested IF gives three levels.

activities.title: Earned value: are we on track?
activities.objective: Compare planned, earned and actual cost to judge schedule and cost performance.
activities.scenario: Halfway through a 200000 rupee project, 40% of the work is complete, 50% was planned and 90000 has been spent. Work out the performance indexes.
steps: In B6 work out planned value: budget times planned percent.
In B7 earned value: budget times percent complete.
In B8 cost variance: earned value minus actual cost.
In B9 schedule variance: earned value minus planned value.
In B10 cost performance index: earned value divided by actual cost.
In B11 schedule performance index: earned value divided by planned value.
In B12 forecast total cost: budget divided by the cost performance index.

checks.label: B10 is CPI
checks.explain: Below 1 means paying more than the value earned.

checks.label: B12 is the forecast cost
checks.explain: If efficiency continues, the final cost rises.

activities.title: Final project: a one-page project plan
activities.objective: Combine charter, scope, schedule, budget, risks and communication into one plan.
activities.scenario: Plan a college tech fest for 500 students with a budget of 2 lakh rupees and a date three months away.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Project plan: College tech fest'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Goal, Scope, Milestones, Budget, Risks, Communication.
Under Milestones write a numbered list of at least four milestones with dates.
Under Risks list at least three risks, each with a response.
Under Budget list at least four cost lines with rupee amounts.
Keep it between 170 and 360 words.

checks.label: Six sections
checks.explain: A plan covers all the knowledge areas briefly.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: Goal, Scope, Milestones, Budget, Risks, Communication.

At least three risks in a list
Risk responses
